generation.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Electric Power Monthly (Form EIA-923), net generation by state and source, grouped by the ERW (docs/methods/generation_mix.md)
generation.hourly_reason: No public source gives a state's generation by the hour; the hourly picture is by balancing authority, in the Grid tool.

retail.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-861M, retail sales and average price by state and sector
retail.revenue_note: Revenue is EIA's sales times EIA's average price for the same month and sector. EIA computes its average price as revenue over sales, so the product gives EIA's revenue to within the price's rounding (one tenth of a dollar a MWh).

plants.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory (Form EIA-860M)
plants.unit: MW (nameplate and net summer); MWh (storage energy)

largest.name: Fore River Generating Station
largest.operator: Calpine Fore River Energy Center, LLC

plants.retired_note: EIA-860M's retired sheet as the ERW's table holds it: the generators retired in its window, not every retirement since 2001.

co2.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, emissions by state by fuel
co2.unit: metric tons of CO2; kg of CO2 per MWh

gas.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Natural Gas Monthly, consumption by end use and production by state
gas.production_reason: EIA prints no marketed production for Massachusetts: it is not a producing state in the Natural Gas Monthly

energy.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Energy Data System

by_sector_reason.commercial: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the commercial sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy
by_sector_reason.transportation: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the transportation sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy

disposition.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, source and disposition
disposition.note: Net interstate trade is EIA's figure: positive where the state took in more electricity from other states than it sent out.

serving.source: U.S. Census Bureau county population estimates, and Form EIA-861's utilities and balancing authorities by county, as the ERW's table eia_county_region joins them
serving.basis: Each county counts once, whole, for its primary authority: the one whose utilities serve most of the county's customers in EIA-861. A county two authorities share is counted for its primary one.

large_load_laws.source: The ERW's large-load research files, each law read at its legislature's or regulator's own page

laws.title: An Act relative to energy affordability, clean power and economic competitiveness
laws.threshold: a data center is a facility designed to have a load of not less than 20 MW
